chunks: The saying of Abī Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام:
"There is no harm in a man speaking during the obligatory salat (prayer) with anything by which he privately converses with his Lord, Mighty and Majestic."

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ الثَّانِي: Imam Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Jawād عليه السلام
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression of permissibility
key_terms.لِقَوْلِ: indicating that what follows is a reported saying
key_terms.يُنَاجِي: he confidentially converses or supplicates intimately

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to speak to Allah in one's own words during the obligatory salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that there is no harm in speaking within the obligatory salat (prayer) in words that constitute intimate discourse with Allah, exalted is He. It indicates the permissibility of utterances in prayer when they are directed to one's Lord as devotion and supplication.
